root_cause.text: In nouveau_drm_probe(), the error path after nvkm_device_pci_new() incorrectly returned مباشرة on aperture_remove_conflicting_pci_devices() failure instead of unwinding the already-created nvkm_device, causing a resource leak of the nvkm_device and its pci_enable_device() reference.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (ret) return ret;` to `if (ret) goto fail_nvkm;`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that on aperture removal failure “the error path returns directly without unwinding the nvkm_device that was just allocated by nvkm_device_pci_new()”, leaking “both the device wrapper and the pci_enable_device() reference taken inside it.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Route aperture-removal failures through the nvkm cleanup path in nouveau_drm_probe() to avoid leaking initialized resources on probe error.
intent_record.what: In nouveau_drm_probe(), the error path after aperture_remove_conflicting_pci_devices(pdev, driver_pci.name) was changed from immediately returning ret to jumping to the fail_nvkm label with goto fail_nvkm.
intent_record.how: On failure from aperture_remove_conflicting_pci_devices(), execution now follows the shared cleanup path associated with fail_nvkm instead of exiting directly, ensuring previously initialized nvkm-related resources are released before returning the error.

grouping_result.intent: Route aperture-removal failures through the nvkm cleanup path in nouveau_drm_probe() to avoid leaking initialized resources on probe error.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it alters nouveau_drm_probe() so aperture_remove_conflicting_pci_devices() failures go through the nvkm cleanup path, preventing the leaked nvkm_device and pci_enable_device() reference on probe error.

candidates.rationale: This direct return on aperture_remove_conflicting_pci_devices() failure exits nouveau_drm_probe() without unwinding the already-created nvkm_device, causing the resource leak described in the root cause.
This condition gates the faulty error path; when aperture_remove_conflicting_pci_devices() fails, execution takes the immediate return path instead of jumping to nvkm cleanup.

vuln_statements.explanation: This direct return is the faulty error-path behavior. When aperture_remove_conflicting_pci_devices() fails after nvkm_device_pci_new() has already created the nvkm_device, returning here skips the unwind/cleanup path, leaking the nvkm_device and its pci_enable_device() reference.

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nouveau_drm.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nouveau_drm.c
index ca4087f5a15b..eb10c80ed853 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nouveau_drm.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nouveau_drm.c
@@ -681,8 +68
bic_trace_step.reason: The root cause describes a leak when the first nvkm_device created by nvkm_device_pci_new() is still live when aperture_remove_conflicting_pci_devices()/remove_conflicting_pci_framebuffers() fails, and the function returns directly without unwinding it. In this snippet, that first temporary device is explicitly destroyed before the conflicting-framebuffer removal call: lines 692-695 create it with `ret = nvkm_device_pci_new(..., &device);` and `if (ret) return ret;`, then line 697 immediately calls `nvkm_device_del(&device);`. Only after that does the code call `remove_conflicting_pci_framebuffers()` on lines 700-702, and on failure it does `return ret;`. Because the temporary `device` has already been deleted before this return path, the vulnerable construct (returning with a live nvkm_device still allocated) is absent. The later second `nvkm_device_pci_new()` at lines 704-705 is covered by the `fail_nvkm:` unwind path at lines 744-745. Therefore the function already contains the fix-relevant handling and does not exhibit the described leak.
